issues.description: Time/identity semantics of the response-bookend are complected with a 1-second sleep
issues.detail: The processor uses wall-clock timeout to decide when an LLM response ends, then also closes deterministically after the stream finishes. Two different time models (timer vs. stream-completion) are intertwined in one piece of mutable state (_output_response_open). Since process_frame already knows when the stream ends, drop the timer entirely: emit Start before the loop, Text inside, End after. One concept, no race.

issues.description: A new boto3 client is constructed per invocation inside process_frame
issues.detail: The async with block creates and tears down a bedrock-agentcore client for every LLMContextFrame. That complects connection lifecycle with request handling and adds incidental latency. The identity here (the client) should be created once at processor start and reused; the values (payloads, responses) flow through it.

issues.description: SSE parsing is hand-rolled and complects framing with content extraction
issues.detail: The code splits on newlines, checks 'data: ' prefix, slices [6:], warns on mismatch, and only then hands the payload to a transformer. Wire framing (SSE) and semantic extraction (response JSON) are two concerns. Decompose: a small pure function lines -> events, then transformer event -> text. Easier to test, and the 'data: ' magic number disappears.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer will raise on any non-JSON line
issues.detail: json.loads(response_line) has no try/except. A heartbeat, blank keepalive, or malformed line from the agent will throw out of process_frame and leave _output_response_open=True with a dangling close_task. Either guard the parse and return None on failure, or document that transformers must be total functions over the input space.

issues.description: agentArn parameter name violates Python convention and complects AWS wire naming with the public API
issues.detail: The constructor takes agentArn (camelCase) because that's what the AWS SDK field is called, but every other kwarg is snake_case. The boto3 field name is an incidental detail of the transport; the processor's API is a separate concern. Rename to agent_arn and pass it through as agentRuntimeArn at the call site.

issues.description: Module docstring and class name disagree (AWSAgentCoreProcessor vs AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor in PR title)
issues.detail: The PR title says AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor; the code exports AWSAgentCoreProcessor. Small thing, but the name is the value users import; pick one and align docs, class, and PR. Names are values too.

review.summary: The core processor is mostly straightforward request/response, but it has gratuitously complected the simple thing (stream in, frames out) with a timer-based bookend mechanism that races against the deterministic end-of-stream path. The 1-second asyncio.sleep is COMPLECTED time semantics: two different notions of "response is over" sharing one boolean. Decompose: Start before the loop, Text inside, End after, no timer, no _close_task. Secondary concerns: per-request client construction (identity vs. value confusion), hand-rolled SSE parsing that mixes framing with extraction, and an un-guarded json.loads in the default transformer that will crash on any non-JSON keepalive. The bones are fine; the incidental complexity is removable.
